Why third-party scripts are performance killers

Third-party scripts (analytics, chat, A/B testing, tag managers, ad networks) are outside your control yet run on your user's main thread. HTTPArchive data: average page loads 21 third-party scripts. These block rendering, consume CPU, and can introduce single points of failure. Your page load is only as fast as the slowest third-party CDN.

⚠️ Render blocking
<script> without async/defer blocks HTML parsing. 1 slow CDN = page blank for 3+ seconds
⚡ Long Tasks
Tag manager + analytics + chat = 400KB JS. Each initialises eagerly, consuming main thread during user interaction
🏥 SPOF risk
If analytics CDN is down and script blocks, page never loads for users. Must always be async + fallback

Loading strategies (in order of best to worst)

Facade pattern — load a placeholder (iframe/div) first, inject real 3rd-party script only on user interaction (hover/click). Best for chat, maps, video.
defer + user-visible timing — inject script after INP-critical path. Use Intersection Observer or requestIdleCallback.
async attribute — doesn't block HTML parsing, but still executes as soon as loaded (may interrupt at bad time).
Synchronous <script> — blocks HTML parser at insertion point. Never use for third-party scripts.

Facade pattern + idle loading

// Facade pattern for chat widget (Intercom / Drift)
function loadChatOnce() {
  if (window._chatLoaded) return;
  window._chatLoaded = true;
  const s = document.createElement('script');
  s.src = 'https://widget.intercom.io/widget/APP_ID';
  s.async = true;
  document.head.appendChild(s);
}
// Only load when user hovers or clicks the chat button
document.getElementById('chat-btn')
  .addEventListener('mouseenter', loadChatOnce, { once: true });

// Defer analytics until after user interaction (Next.js pattern)
// next.config.js Script component with strategy
// <Script src="..." strategy="afterInteractive" /> — loads after hydration
// <Script src="..." strategy="lazyOnload" />   — loads during idle time
// <Script src="..." strategy="worker" />       — moves to Web Worker (Partytown)

// Partytown — run third-party scripts in Web Worker thread
// yarn add @builder.io/partytown
import { Partytown } from '@builder.io/partytown/react';
// In _app.tsx:
<Partytown debug={process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'} forward={['dataLayer.push']} />
<script type="text/partytown" src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js" />

// CSP to restrict what third-party scripts can do
// Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://www.googletagmanager.com;
